look_here_first: SOUTHWESTERN / SCHEELE'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): a tall, commonly broad-leaved and hairy grass with a long, tapered, rather open bottlebrush-like head. Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) LONG separate projecting bristles per spikelet, typically 10–35 mm in FNA/Kew. Unlike Reverchon's shorter sparse bristles, these long bristles are actually obvious in the saved flowering photograph. Edwards Plateau shady limestone canyon habitat is supportive, not conclusive.

best_field_traits: SOUTHWESTERN / SCHEELE'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): a tall, commonly broad-leaved and hairy grass with a long, tapered, rather open bottlebrush-like head. Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) LONG separate projecting bristles per spikelet, typically 10–35 mm in FNA/Kew. Unlike Reverchon's shorter sparse bristles, these long bristles are actually obvious in the saved flowering photograph. Edwards Plateau shady limestone canyon habitat is supportive, not conclusive.
Coarse warm-season perennial bunchgrass with rhizomatous/rooted base, often fairly tall, sometimes exceeding 1 m.
Relatively broad, pubescent foliage with prominent midvein, often about 5–18 mm wide.
Conspicuous elongate single terminal bottlebrush-like flowering head; Texas A&M describes inflorescence about 15–35 cm long.
Spikelets generally about 2.1–2.6 mm in regional treatments, often associated with a single conspicuous long bristle.
Bristles are sterile reduced branchlets NOT a true awn of the floret; study both bristle and tiny spikelet.
Edwards Plateau limestone canyons/open woods and partially shaded areas are useful habitat cues, not proof of species or county nativity.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole rooted perennial clump with broad hairy foliage and long tapering head, ruler
Macro of 1 (sometimes up to 3) bristles arising at individual spikelet base, 1-mm ruler
10–35 mm intact long bristle with attached 2.2–2.5 mm mature spikelet on same head
Leaf collar ligule 1–2 mm and broad pubescent blade with true width scale
Rhizome/culm base and mature panicle matched on same specimen
crew_field_check: First find the WHOLE panicle and compare crowded/loose head arrangement without forcing species from silhouette.
Inspect an intact attached SPIKELET at 10–20×. Count the SUBTENDING PERSISTENT BRISTLES (sterile branches), not grass awns or protruding flower parts.
Record bristle count/length and spikelet length using a 1-mm scale, and compare the same-plant collar ligule.
Check a rooted base only where collecting is legal: annual fibrous millet vs knotty rhizomatous perennial parviflora/reverchonii, and perennial scheelei.
Existing archival images do not prove every underlying bristle count or rhizome; if unresolved identify Setaria sp.
next_photo_sequence_20261023: Verify existing three JPEGs display on the ordinary public species gallery; inspect actual image pixels before assigning anatomy markers.
Get rooted whole plant with head and foliage visible, not only one detached head.
Show entire attached inflorescence and several spikelet base close-ups.
Photograph attached collar true hair-fringe ligule with 1 mm ruler.
Photograph attached mature spikelet plus persistent sterile-branchlet bristles and 1 mm scale; record species-appropriate numbers and measurements.
Finish with matched Setaria reverchonii, scheelei and parviflora comparative head/base photo, arrows only on clearly resolved structures.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Conspicuously projecting mostly solitary ~10–35 mm bristles on an elongate tapered head distinguish S. scheelei from sparse/shorter-bristled interrupted S. reverchonii and the many-bristled short rhizomatous S. parviflora. Annual foxtail millet S. italica can have a long head but usually denser/lobed cultivated seedheads, broad foliage and nonperennial roots. Check at least several mature spikelets; bristles are sterile branches, NOT awns.
not_reliable_alone: Color or texture of seedhead without bristle group macro
Bristles mistaken for true floret awns or flower stigmas
Mature spikelet counts read from a photo too small to show attachment
Cultivated or habitat context presented as confirmed local nativity

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: Look for a perennial tuft with broad often hairy blades and long TAPERING, relatively loose bottlebrush head. At a mature spikelet base find usually ONE conspicuous projecting bristle ~10–35 mm; that bristle is a sterile branchlet, NOT a floret awn.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_growth_and_collar: Perennial cespitose grass with culms ~60–120(125) cm, often hairy nodes, broad blades ~5–18 mm in Texas sources. True ligule a ~1–2-mm hair fringe, collar pilose; inspect the actual blade/sheath junction separately from sheath hairs.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_inflorescence_and_bristles: Long tapering open spike-like panicle ~15–25 cm in FNA/Kew, to ~35 cm in Texas A&M; usually 1, occasionally 2–3, persistent bristles per spikelet, ~10–35 mm, divergent. Spikelets ovate ~2.2–2.5 mm, with one sterile lower and one fertile upper floret.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_spikelet_glumes_lemmas_awns: Lower glume about half spikelet length, 3-veined; upper glume about 3/4 to near fertile-floret length, 5-veined. Lower sterile lemma near upper lemma length, 5-veined; lower palea present and about half upper palea length in FNA. Fertile upper lemma firm, finely cross-wrinkled, shortly pointed; no long true glume/lemma awns. Long conspicuous structures are persistent sterile-branch bristles.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: S. reverchonii has a slender interrupted head and sparse shorter bristles (~2–8 mm when present); S. parviflora has short dense heads, hard knotty rhizomes and many (4–12) shorter bristles per spikelet; cultivated S. italica is annual and often much denser. Edwards Plateau limestone canyon habitat supports but cannot certify identification.
last_mile_photo_holds: One rooted species-vetted perennial with hairy blade, collar and full tapering flowering head, cm scale.
Multiple 10–20× spikelets each showing attached one versus occasional 2–3 basal 10–35-mm bristles and a mm ruler; existing overview bristles are not a countable attachment voucher.
Measured 1–2-mm true hair-fringe ligule and collar at the attached sheath/blade junction.
Dissected glumes, sterile lemma/palea and finely cross-wrinkled upper lemma with mm scale, plus matched S. reverchonii comparison.

items.label: Foxtail millet — dense, nodding cultivated seedheads
items.image_role: Real existing garden/crop overview showing branching millet head silhouette rather than microscopic identity
items.caption: Original credited overview shows multiple long densely packed, at times curved and drooping foxtail-millet heads with relatively wide leaves. It cannot expose individual basal bristle counts, ligules, exact millimeters or true annual root system.
items.why_it_matters: FOXTAIL MILLET (INTRODUCED annual crop/escape): start with stout annual culms, broad foliage, and a heavy dense often lobed or nodding foxtail head. Flora of North America usually describes 1–3 persistent subtending bristles (to ~12 mm), NOT 'numerous bristles beneath every spikelet'. A crop-derived head varies greatly; distinguish from perennial native bristlegrasses using rooted duration, panicle shape and ripe spikelets.

items.why_it_matters: KNOTROOT BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): FIRST verify a living short hard knotty basal rhizome, then a generally short even-width dense foxtail head (~3–8 cm). FNA reports 4–12 persistent bristles, 2–12 mm long, beneath each spikelet; they must be counted from a genuinely intact head at 10–20×. Our only stored macro shows green bracts and pink emergent floral tissue with a 2-mm scale, NOT the perennial rhizome or a countable group of 4–12 basal bristles.

items.why_it_matters: REVERCHON'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): the existing real photo shows a skinny, often interrupted upright flowering head, with widely separated spikelet groupings. Its bristles are sparse—some spikelets appear almost unbristled—but FNA gives bristles about 2–8 mm where present; do NOT teach a hard ≤2 mm cutoff. Seek short knotty rhizomes, the stiff hair ligule (1–2 mm), and mature 2.1–4.5 mm spikelets. No bristle measurement is visible in the original picture.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Setaria — the bristle count is on a real spikelet
steps: START with the Kyla Miller archived photo: locate the long tapered flowering axis and conspicuous long outward projecting bristles. The three existing arrows mark visible gross structures, not counted spikelet attachments.
COMPARE THE EXTRA TWO ARCHIVED PHOTOS: CC0 Gaiacoyote and CC BY Annika Lindqvist source-labelled images are available in this same gallery. Do not add another head shot merely for photo count.

COUNT BRISTLES AT ONE ATTACHED RIPE SPIKELET under 10–20×: usually one, sometimes two or three distinct persistent sterile branch bristles; DO NOT confuse long bristles with true lemma awns. Literature lengths about 10–35 mm, not measured from the current photographs.

OPEN THE SAME SPIKELET against 1-mm scale: often 2.2–2.5 mm long; lower glume three-veined, upper glume five-veined; lower sterile lemma approximately five-veined; firm fertile upper lemma subtly cross-wrinkled. These microscopic parts are currently UNPHOTOGRAPHED.
UNFOLD the TRUE COLLAR on a mature leaf: measure 1–2-mm hair-fringe ligule separately from collar and sheath hairs. A broad hairy blade by itself cannot confirm the ligule.

MATCH ROOTED PERENNIAL BASE, broad often hairy leaves, and entire relatively loose tapered flowering head from the SAME individual. Compare S. reverchonii (often interrupted narrower head with sparse shorter bristles), S. parviflora (more numerous basal bristles, knotty rhizomes), and cultivated S. italica (dense annual head).

FIELD HOLD: retain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until a legally collected/photographed specimen gives real bristle insertion, attached fertile spikelet/glume details and a scaled ligule. Never aim new arrows at structures absent from the pixels.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: LONG conspicuous projecting mostly solitary bristles + relatively loose tapered foxtail panicle + hairy broad leaves; confirm the SINGLE bristle attachment and tiny hair-fringed ligule.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: 3 exact-source JPEGs locally archived, all three gallery views included, existing three gross-structure arrows untouched. No authenticated close-up proves the number of bristles subtending a single spikelet, glume veins, or 1–2-mm ligule. NPS documents a public-domain policy conditional on photographer credit; its separate photo is a candidate only, not added until its exact rights and anatomical role are reviewed. Existing CC BY-NC preserved.
